paras: The shooting of an escaping prisoner in Savannah took place on the evening of 26 August 1881, when an officer taking an unnamed Black man to jail fired at him as he ran and hit him in the thigh. The wounded man was recaptured and returned to the jail, and the Savannah Morning News reported the incident in a brief local item the next morning.

About half-past six in the evening, an officer was "carrying a negro to jail" when the prisoner made a sudden jump, broke free of the officer's grasp and "darted down the street." A shot from a Smith & Wesson revolver was fired after him and struck him in the thigh, which, in the paper's words, "compelled him to stop." He was then "easily captured" and taken back to the jail.
The item does not name the prisoner or the officer, does not say why he was being arrested, and does not name the street, though it ran among the paper's Savannah local news.

The paper said it was "impossible to learn any further particulars beyond the fact that the negro had been shot," and no follow-up report, inquiry or account of the wounded man's condition appears in the coverage.

The only known report is the Savannah Morning News item of 27 August 1881, headed "An Escaping Prisoner Shot." Told entirely from the standpoint of the arrest, it called the wounded man a "fugitive darkey" and presented the shot as the end of an escape attempt, without questioning the use of the revolver. No report of the shooting in any other paper appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: Savannah Morning News local item
accounts.gist: The prisoner made a sudden jump, freed himself and ran; a revolver shot hit him in the thigh and stopped him, and he was returned to jail. The paper could learn nothing further.
